land.text: the Santa Elena peninsula; the page lists only 'Followed by: Machalilla culture, Cotocollao culture' and gives no land for either

successors.note: Cotocollao is in the Quito highlands and is not the same land.

correction.text: "thrived along the coast of Santa Elena peninsula in Santa Elena Province of Ecuador"; infobox "Geographical range: Santa Elena"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox "Dates: 3800 - 1500 BC"; the prose "thrived along the coast of Santa Elena peninsula in Santa Elena Province of Ecuador between 3500 BC and 1500 BC". The province is a fair stand-in for the peninsula (13 land cells); the page lists later sites at Real Alto, Salango, Loma Alta, Colimes and San Lorenzo del Mate without dates, so they are not drawn. No area is given.

region.text: "thrived along the coast of Santa Elena peninsula in Santa Elena Province of Ecuador"; infobox "Geographical range: Santa Elena"

ledger.note: 3800 BCE: the Valdivia culture begins on the coast of the Santa Elena peninsula, Ecuador. Infobox "Dates: 3800 - 1500 BC" and "Preceded by: Las Vegas culture"; the prose has it thriving "between 3500 BC and 1500 BC" and "one thousand years after the Las Vegas culture". The dossier takes the infobox start; the 3500 BC date is the prose's.

3000 BCE: Valdivia ceramic Phase A. "Phase A of the Valdivia was long thought to be the oldest pottery produced by a coastal culture" and is "dated to 3000-2700 BC"; the older "San Pedro" pottery pre-dates it.

region.text: "thrived along the coast of Santa Elena peninsula in Santa Elena Province of Ecuador"; infobox "Geographical range: Santa Elena"

ledger.note: 1500 BCE: the Valdivia culture ends and the Machalilla culture follows. Infobox "Dates: 3800 - 1500 BC" and "Followed by: Machalilla culture, Cotocollao culture"; the page gives no land for the Machalilla, so the hand-over of the Santa Elena coast is the dossier's reading.

certainty.note: No border is recorded; the coast of the Santa Elena peninsula is the only extent the page names.

sources.title: Valdivia culture

sources.title: Real Alto
sources.note: Real Alto in Santa Elena: settled 6000-3800 BC; "the start of Valdivia culture at 5600 BP (3600 BC)"; Valdivia town of about 1,250 people c. 2500 BCE.

notes: Valdivia culture, Santa Elena, Ecuador. Infobox "Dates: 3800 - 1500 BC" against prose "between 3500 BC and 1500 BC": start -3800 follows the infobox. The Las Vegas culture (predecessor) was not opened (the Wikipedia title "Las Vegas culture" is the Nevada city and the variants tried did not load), so Ecuador before 3800 BCE is blank. Machalilla (successor) has no dossier. Page area: none. Third start date: the Real Alto page (opened 2026-10-18) has "the start of Valdivia culture at 5600 BP (3600 BC)" and says Real Alto "was settled between 6000 and 3800 BC", with "Region: Santa Elena, Ecuador", so the Santa Elena coast was occupied before the infobox start of Valdivia by a pre-Valdivian people the page does not name (the Valdivia infobox says "Preceded by: Las Vegas culture"); Santa Elena -6000..-3801 is therefore blank here although occupied, and a Las Vegas culture dossier is needed (no page of that title loaded). Around 2500 BCE the Valdivia town of Real Alto reached "about 1,250 individuals".
